The paper itself establishes n_opt in {3..10}, so letters above each item's n_opt are ILLEGAL. Because the balanced-10 null spreads mass over ten letters where legal data concentrates it on fewer, it depresses both E[f_hat] and q95 and therefore overstates significance.
issues.required_action: Re-run the E-CAL calibration for BOTH MMLU-Pro rows with each item's gold label drawn uniformly over that item's OWN legal letters, same seed (20260814), same draw count, same estimator f_hat=max_L m_hat_L. Second assertion: no simulated draw may place mass on a letter with index >= that item's n_opt. Third: MMLU and BoolQ p-values must be byte-unchanged (fixed k).

issues.my_verification: CONFIRMED by direct recomputation from the frozen tables, no simulation. tab_nulls.tex row 2 prints Chance=0.110877 and E[f_hat]=0.104460 on the same line; the caption and A.1.4 define that Chance as mean(1/n_opt). Letter A is legal on every item (n_opt>=3), so under any legal balanced process E[m_A]=mean(1/n_opt)=0.110877 exactly, and f_hat=max_L m_L >= m_A forces E[f_hat]>=0.110877. The row prints E[f_hat]-Chance = -0.006417: the expectation of a maximum below the expectation of one of its own arguments. I applied the same test to all nine rows: 8/9 pass, the single violation is the MMLU-Pro item-average row, i.e. the paper's flagship. I ALSO CHECKED A NUANCE NO REVIEWER STATED: the 'naive' MMLU-Pro row is NOT self-contradictory, because its Chance is 1/k=0.100, not mean(1/n_opt); the deductive contradiction bites only the item-avg row. issues.title: The only surviving global inferential claim uses a Bin(12,0.05) independence model that the paper itself denies eleven lines earlier
issues.class_reason: A self-contradiction inside one shipped .tex file. Packaging is irrelevant.
issues.diagnosis: 09a_relocated.tex:26: 'the cells share items, nest arms, and share a null, so the tests are neither independent nor exchangeable, and an off-the-shelf Bonferroni or Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment would not have a defensible family definition here.' Eleven lines later the same file computes P(X>=3 | Bin(12,0.05)) = 0.0196 from those same twelve decisions. Dependence is used to decline correction and then ignored to produce a global p-value. Under positive dependence the count's tail is heavier, so 0.0196 is anti-conservative.
issues.required_action: Replace Bin(12,0.05) with an item-level joint null: resample items once, recompute all 12 cells inside each resample, report the rejection-count distribution (the existing 10,000-resample paired-bootstrap machinery does this at no new measurement cost). OR demote 3/12 to a descriptive count and drop the probability. Do not present an independence-based global p while arguing dependence.
issues.verification_test: The reported aggregate p must come from the item-resampled joint distribution, not from Bin(12,0.05); the sentence containing 0.0196 must also carry P(X>=2)=0.1184; report the implied intra-class correlation.
issues.my_verification: CONFIRMED, and I read both sentences verbatim in the frozen 09a_relocated.tex (lines 26 and 44 region; the 0.0196 sentence is duplicated in 05_analysis.tex:25). Exact arithmetic with fractions.Fraction: P(X>=3|Bin(12,1/20)) = 0.019568 (paper prints 0.0196) - correct. The fragility is real and I recomputed it: P(X>=2) = 0.118360, a 6.05x jump that crosses alpha=0.05, so the claim is one cell from vanishing. P(X>=1) = 0.459640, so the floor side's own 1/12 does not clear the bar - which means the paper's chosen statistic is asymmetric in a second way nobody flagged: it is only 'significant' because the chance side happened to land on exactly 3. R-stats' beta-binomial sensitivity (rho=0.05 -> 0.0501, rho=0.10 -> 0.0678) is the sharpest constructive form and I accept it as plausible without independently reproducing the log-Beta computation.

issues.title: v1 is presented as a pre-comparison / interface-validity gate, but subtracting a common constant provably cannot change any arm difference or ordering
issues.severity_note: All four codex reviewers rate major and it is a large part of why their technical_soundness medians are 2. The meta-review reduces the severity to a claim_narrowing fix, noting the paper already retracted the strong form in its own ledger (C-15) and the abstract already says 'necessary, not sufficient'. I keep both positions.
issues.class_reason: Pure algebra plus wording. No evidence file involved.
affected: sections/tab_two_nulls.tex (the v1 column header 'Is this interface valid for comparing arms?')
issues.diagnosis: Delta_floor(A) - Delta_floor(B) = (acc(A)-f) - (acc(B)-f) = acc(A)-acc(B) exactly, so v1 cannot alter a pairwise difference or an ordering. Two arms can have a real reproducible difference while both sit below the floor; a systematically anti-aligned predictor can carry substantial item information at very low accuracy. The paper's own v2 analysis demonstrates that below-floor status is not equivalent to absence of item dependence.
issues.required_action: Narrow v1 from a comparability gate to an absolute above-constant reference. Rewrite the tab_two_nulls v1 question. State in one sentence that a common floor leaves pairwise differences invariant.
issues.verification_test: No sentence in abstract, intro, Section 3.1, any table header, the checklist or the discussion may infer invalidity or incomparability of arm differences from Delta_floor <= 0 alone. Test the wording against two explicit counterexamples: two distinct below-floor predictors, and a perfectly anti-aligned predictor.
issues.my_verification: The algebra is trivially correct and I confirm it. I also checked the mitigating evidence the meta-review cites and it is REAL: the frozen 00_abstract.tex does contain 'This floor is a necessary, not sufficient, validity condition', and the shipped evidence/claim_evidence_map.tsv row C-15 does read 'Clearing the floor certifies validity - Retracted - Clearing is necessary, not sufficient; failure disqualifies, success does not certify.' So the paper has already retracted the strong form in its own ledger. HOWEVER, the four reviewers are pointing at a DIFFERENT sentence: the tab_two_nulls.tex v1 column header still asks 'Is this interface valid for comparing arms?', which asserts exactly the retracted form in a table caption. Both sides are right about different sentences. My reading: the defect is real and localised to wording, and 'the ledger already retracted it' is a reason to fix the surviving instances, not a reason to score it lower.
issues.confidence: very_high (the algebra); the severity is genuinely contested and I preserve it

issues.title: '0/60 damaged cells clear their floor' is offered as near-unanimity while the same sentence says 52/60 are underpowered; the design expects only ~12 detections even if every arm truly cleared

issues.class_reason: It is the paper's own 'Power is part of construct validity' principle applied to the paper's own headline aggregate, using the paper's own printed half-widths.
issues.diagnosis: The paper states twice that its conclusions rest on the aggregate's near-unanimity (0/60 clear their floor) while stating in the same breath that 52/60 are underpowered for the 1.389 pp reference effect. Using tab_power's own five half-widths, expected detections if EVERY arm truly cleared by delta: +0.5 pp -> 3.5/60; +1.0 pp -> 7.6/60; +1.389 pp -> 12.0/60. Observing 0 is therefore consistent with a substantial positive true effect. It is a failure-to-reject presented as near-unanimity - and it is the paper's declared SUBSTITUTE for family-wise correction.
issues.required_action: Accompany 0/60 and 0/15 with the design's expected detection count under a stated alternative (~12/60 at +1.389 pp), or replace the count with a pooled effect and interval.
issues.verification_test: Publish per-cell half-width and implied power at delta=+1.389 pp for all 60 cells plus the summed expected detections (should be ~12). A reader must be able to see that 0/60 excludes delta >= +1.0 pp and does not exclude delta = +0.3 pp.
issues.my_verification: I VERIFIED THE PREMISES AND THE FORM, NOT THE 60 HALF-WIDTHS (they are printed nowhere - see B-11). Verified: the paper does say twice that the conclusions rest on 0/60 (04_experiments.tex:23 verbatim 'the conclusions rest on the aggregate's near-unanimity (0/60 damaged cells clear their floor), not on one cell'; 09a_relocated.tex:26 the same). Verified: 09a_relocated.tex:44 says '52/60 are underpowered'. The two statements are in tension by construction, so the finding follows in form from the paper's own numbers. I could not reproduce 3.5/7.6/12.0/29.3 because they need the 60 half-widths. R-stats explicitly notes the finding is NOT vacuous (P(0/60 | delta=+1.0 pp) = 2e-4), so large effects are genuinely excluded - the defect is the word 'near-unanimity', not the count. IMPORTANT: this issue INTERACTS with B-02. If shortgpt16 belongs in a designated-damaged denominator, then 0/60 and 0/15 are also affected, not just 14/15. disagreements_preserved.topic: Whether the symmetric-standard table (3/12 vs 1/12) still contains the asymmetry it was added to remove

positions.argument: The subsection states the criterion is 'the two-sided 95% interval on BOTH sides'. tab_mmlupro's mid-p values give three sub-0.05 cells: qwen3/k14 p=0.0192 (above), llama2/k8 p=0.0168 (below), qwen3/k8 p=0.0362 (below). The printed 1/12 is reachable only by counting above-side rejections for the floor while counting both sides for chance.

Both call the same subsection exemplary. R-stats states it reconstructed BOTH floor-side counts exactly from tab_mmlupro (point-above = 3/12; CI-excludes-0 = 1/12) and lists the self-correction as a verified strength. R4 calls it 'the single most consequential retraction in the paper'.

DOES NOT ADJUDICATE THIS AT ALL. The meta-review lists the 5.1 self-correction as consensus strength #2 and never engages R1's challenge to it. This is the largest coverage gap I found in the meta-review.

disagreements_preserved.my_adjudication: BOTH ARITHMETICS ARE CORRECT AND THEY COUNT DIFFERENT EVENTS. I recomputed the floor side from tab_mmlupro's own deltas and half-widths: CI excludes 0 in the ABOVE direction = 1/12 (Qwen3 k14 only, CI [+0.042,+0.424]); CI excludes 0 in the BELOW direction = 2/12 (Llama-2 k8 CI [-1.650,-0.178] and Qwen3 k8 CI [-1.700,-0.062]); CI excludes 0 in EITHER direction = 3/12. So the paper's 1/12 counts 'the arm CLEARS its floor' and R1's 3/12 counts 'the cell is RESOLVED in either direction'. Whether R1's symmetry complaint has force depends entirely on what the chance-side 3/12 counts - and THE PER-CELL CHANCE-SIDE DELTAS AND HALF-WIDTHS ARE PRINTED NOWHERE (see B-11d), so THIS IS NOT DECIDABLE FROM THE SNAPSHOT. The required action is the same either way: add per-cell chance-side delta, half-width and p to tab_mmlupro (already required by B-11) and state explicitly which event each column counts. If R1 is right, the paper's single most-quoted contrast weakens from 3/12-vs-1/12 to 3/12-vs-3/12, which would be a materially larger retraction than the one the paper already made.
